$comment: The mg-legs biped, for the drivers that need to know what a foot is.
A profile rather than constants in a driver, because the alternative is
a `steps.py` per mechanism and this repository's whole claim is that the
drivers are parameterized by project rather than copied per project.
Every name here is a BODY in the exported MJCF. A profile that names a
body the model does not have is refused loudly: a foot that resolves to
no geom is never in contact, so every episode would report one permanent

feet.$comment: The toe is part of the foot ON PURPOSE. It is a separate body with a welded joint, and a machine that has rolled forward onto its toe is still standing on that foot rather than swinging it. Counting the toe as part of the foot is what stops a roll being read as a lift.

$step_mm_comment: Horizontal travel between takeoff and landing past which a lift is called a STEP. 10 mm is about a fifth of this machine's 49 mm half-stance: smaller than that and the foot came down where it left, which is a hop or a shuffle and not a step out.
$min_airborne_comment: How long a foot must be continuously out of contact before the interval counts as a lift at all. 30 ms is longer than any single-step contact chatter the solver produces and far shorter than the 100-300 ms a real swing lasts. A DURATION, not a step count -- see harness/_steps.py:min_airborne_steps for what that cost.
$actuator_comment: MG90S continuous-duty judgment, ~40% of the 216 N*mm stall rating. It models the HARDWARE (method.md section 5). Stated here so a driver can print '% of rating' without a mechanism-specific constant.

support_polygon_mm.$comment: Asymmetric front to back because the toe reaches forward and the heel does not. Measured off the sole and toe geoms of the export, not read off the drawing.
$FRAME_WARNING: THESE THREE NUMBERS ARE NOT IN THE SAME FRAME, and a consumer that
treats them as one polygon around the centre of mass will be wrong.
Re-derived from the compiled model on sb1x, 2026-08-06 (experiment 006
Phase A):
* 45.5 / 24.5 are the sole's reach measured from the ANKLE BRACKET
origin. The foot body sits 12.25 mm forward of it, so the same box
in the FOOT's own frame is +33.25 forward / -36.75 back.
* 50.0 is the DOUBLE-SUPPORT half-width -- the stance spans two feet
60 mm apart. One sole is only +-20 mm wide.
Measured from the CENTRE OF MASS at the `solved` keyframe, which is the
frame a capture point or a centre of pressure actually lives in, the
margins are:  forward 40.83, backward 29.17, lateral 50.00 mm.
This cost a real conclusion. `script.py:2448` sizes the disturbance
band by treating 24.5 as the CoM-relative backward margin AND by
treating the whole +-60 deg shove arc as facing it, and reports that
58 % of aimed draws demand a step. Against the real polygon it is
17.4 %: the margin is 29.17 mm rather than 24.5, and at +-60 deg
off-axis it is 57.7 mm, nearly double. ADR-107 one level down.
`mechanisms/mg-legs/drivers/jitter.py` derives the per-foot box from
the model's own geoms and prints these declared numbers beside it,
labelled, rather than using them.
